winners_curse_rule: pilot effects from 3 v 3 are biased upward and imprecise (Browne 1995, doi:10.1002/sim.4780141709). A pilot effect is never the sizing effect: it is marked on the curve at its point (optimistic) and its conservative value (the more pessimistic of half the point and the 80 % bound nearer zero). Nuisance values (SD, dispersion) are taken at their pessimistic end (the larger of 1.5 x the pilot value and the 80 % upper bound), and the study is sized on the pre-stated effect at that value, with the pilot-point n beside it as the optimistic bound.

T1.test: Welch two-sample t on the logit fraction; equal n and equal SD, so base R power.t.test (strict, two-sided) on 2n - 2 df; pwr::pwr.t.test cross-check
T1.pilot_sd_source: pilot.json#T1_tumour_share.rna_graft_share.pooled_within_arm_sd_logit (RNA human-read share, the only by-species quantity measured without an estimator in between; expression-weighted, not a cell fraction)
T1.conservative_rule: nuisance SD, pessimistic = upward: the larger of 1.5 x the pilot SD (TARGETS sensitivity arm) and the upper bound of its 80 % two-sided chi-square interval (df 4); the study is sized on the pre-stated effect at this SD. The pilot EFFECT is never the sizing effect (TARGETS rule); it is marked on the curve with its point value (optimistic) and its conservative value (the more pessimistic of half the point and the 80 % bound nearer zero)

pilot_effect.source: pilot.json#T1_tumour_share.rna_graft_share.effect_logit and .effect_pp (recurrent minus primary, unablated primary arm; the nearest analogue of ii vs i, not the same contrast)
pilot_effect.reading: the pilot point (15.7 pp) sits on the pre-stated 15 pp target; its conservative value (2.9 pp, the 80 % bound nearer zero) lies below the pre-stated meaningful effect, so it is reported as the power the sized study keeps against it, not used to size

T1b.method: t interval on the logit (n - 1 df) at the pilot or conservative between-rat SD, back-transformed at a 50 % arm mean (the widest point); half of the back-transformed width

T2a.interval: Wilson 95 % score interval at x = n p (formula); binom::binom.confint(methods = 'wilson') at integer x = round(n p) as the cross-check
T2a.pilot_note: the pilot's 1 of 2 was called on sequencing and array evidence, not on the pre-stated IHC + Alu criterion, and both hemispheres come from unablated rats
T2a.conservative_rule: for an interval-width target the pessimistic frequency is the one with the widest interval, 0.50, which is also the pilot point (1 of 2); the anchor 0.20 is the pre-stated sizing frequency and 0.50 the conservative one

T2b.test: Fisher's exact, two-sided; power by exact enumeration over every 2x2 table (R's fisher.test p-value rule)
T2b.pilot: arm ii contralateral NOT SAMPLED in the pilot (both sampled hemispheres are from unablated rats): no pilot effect exists for T2b; the pre-stated contrasts govern
T2b.n_rule: Fisher power saw-tooths in n; n_first_crossing is the smallest n with power >= 0.80, n_stable the smallest n from which every larger n on the grid (to 200) keeps it; the design uses n_stable

T2c.method: one-sided 95 % Clopper-Pearson upper bound with zero positives, 1 - 0.05^(1/n); binom.test cross-check
T2c.pilot: NONE: the pilot has no naive rat, no cutting-order control and no blank library

T3.test: Fisher's exact, two-sided, exact enumeration; Holm over 40 arm-level tests, sized at the worst Holm step 0.05/40
T3.pilot_note: zero recurrence-specific arm events in 3 recurrences; a zero leaves nothing to halve, so the pre-stated prevalences govern

T6.rule: replicates per level n = (z * sd / 0.02)^2 as pre-stated (z = 1.96), and the t form (smallest n with t(0.975, n-1) sd / sqrt(n) <= 0.02) beside it
T6.per_level_sd: UNKNOWN until the titration series is run: the panel is replicates needed against an assumed SD
T6.marked_sd_nearest_measured_is: the CURVE estimator's calibrated leave-one-batch-out mean absolute error on 28 REAL human:MOUSE mixtures (pilot.json#T6_titration.nearest_measured_error.calibrated_leave_one_batch_out.MAE): an error across mixtures, estimator bias included, on a different host; an upper reference, not a replicate SD
T6.detection_limit_definition: the lowest mixture level whose estimate's 95 % interval excludes the pure-rat level; reported as measured, not asserted
T6.arrays_note: 8 mixture levels plus pure RNU brain = 9 arrays per replicate set (8 if the 0 % level is the pure RNU brain itself)

T7.test: Welch t on the composite; equal n, so base R power.t.test (strict) with sd = 1 and delta = d; pwr::pwr.t.test cross-check

pilot.conservative_is: the 80 % bound nearer zero, which crosses zero: the pilot does not support an effect in this direction at 80 % confidence
pilot.reading: the pilot contrast is recurrent vs primary, both tumour-bearing: not the T7 contrast (arms iv and v do not exist in the pilot). Its d is shown for context only; d is scale-free, so the pilot supplies no nuisance parameter for T7

T8.interval: Wilson 95 % lower bound on the share of animals rejecting in the pre-stated direction (SchwingNet Figure 5a construction)
T8.per_animal_rejection_probability: UNKNOWN: it depends on the barcode bottleneck, which no published source gives for intracranial U251N; the curves below assume values, marked as assumptions
T8.detection_floor_rule: recovered barcodes per compartment per animal are measured and reported per animal; the detection floor for N1 and N2 is fixed before unblinding from the injectate's sequenced frequency vector
T8.seed_note: no simulation enters T8's numbers: the level-2 bound and the probability of meeting it are exact binomial; the level-1 permutation seed is fixed in the analysis plan, not here
T8.level1_power: UNKNOWN until the bottleneck is measured

covariate_cost.formula: variance inflation of the arm effect after adjusting for tumour fraction = 1 / (1 - r^2) = 1 + d^2 / 4 for two equal arms, d = standardised arm difference in the covariate
covariate_cost.note: an approximation for the negative-binomial and limma models (exact for the linear model); the rats the covariate costs are the rats needed without it times the inflation, rounded up

ii.label: tumour + LITT, harvest at MRI regrowth

iii.label: tumour + LITT, early harvest in the treatment-effect window

totals.T6_animals: the RNU brain DNA for the titration comes from arm-v rats; no extra animal
totals.rule_conservative: per arm, the largest n over the targets read on it: confirmatory targets at the Holm worst-step alpha 0.0167, T3 at 0.05/40, T4 and T5 at 1.5 x pilot dispersion or the 80 % upper bound of the pilot beta SD with the fraction covariate at its pessimistic inflation, T2a at frequency 0.50, T8 at the 0.80 bound
totals.rule_unadjusted: the same targets at alpha 0.05 without the Holm step, T3 without the 40-test step, T4/T5 without the covariate, T2a at the anchor 0.20
totals.rule_optimistic: the pilot point nuisance values and the largest pre-stated effect curve; shown beside, never used to size
three_Rs: arms iv and v are sized for T7 only; they are not carried to the tumour arms' n
T2c's 29 tumour-free control pieces come from arm-v hemispheres and arm-iv contralateral hemispheres already in the design; no extra animal
T6's RNU brain DNA comes from an arm-v rat; no extra animal

T8 runs inside arm ii when every implant uses the barcoded U251N and at least the T8 number of arm-ii rats carry a pre-LITT sample (0 extra animals); if the pre-LITT sample could perturb the arm-ii endpoints, T8 becomes a separate barcoded sub-arm at the 0.80 bound
arm iii is sized for estimation (T1b, T2a) only, because no confirmatory contrast reads it

attrition.pilot_loss: IL64B held no tumour; rat 65 gave no library (RESUME.md, limits)
attrition.note: an allowance for attrition is a design decision the protocol states; the pilot's 2 of 8 is too imprecise to set it. Enrolment if that loss rate held = n / 0.75

table.quantity: DMP power 0.80 at delta-beta 0.10, fraction covariate
